names: DoD2 breaking checklist covers every legacy command and every config group
cp3 README contains every breaking mapping, both upgrade choices and explicit recovery boundaries
DoD1 originals and copied sources keep exact digests across export and import
cp1 SQLite and bundle exports are stable and preserve raw payloads and recorded hashes
DoD1 unknown SQLite version is explicitly refused with no source writes
cp1 unmarked v1, foreign tables, extra columns and unreadable SQLite are refused
cp1 WAL/journal snapshots and unavailable files are refused rather than silently losing data
cp1 all four YAML document formats are explicit, strict and preserve omitted defaults
cp1 unknown YAML/bundle versions, unknown keys, duplicates and malformed input reject
cp1 non-JSON YAML, cyclic aliases and invalid UTF-8 refuse without source mutation
cp2 import is idempotent with per-record source digest, time and importer version
cp2 all six formats import independently and remain readable without the old source
DoD2 old accepted ledger remains historical and cannot enter journal or asset qualification
cp2 tampered export bytes, records, versions and execution flags reject before creating state
cp2 immutable conflicts and damaged archive retry fail without replacement
cp2 restart reuses a committed archive and ignores interrupted pending files
cp2 actual process termination before publication recovers through explicit retry
cp3 source directory, namespace links and source hardlinks never become write targets
cp3 altered per-record provenance and execution metadata are refused on archive read

real negative control source-writeback: green -> red -> restored green
real negative control history-as-execution-evidence: green -> red -> restored green
real negative control breaking-command-omitted: green -> red -> restored green
